fixes.explanation: Right on the money, baker. The text says he must make restitution by "…adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest…" (Leviticus 5:16). That's the value plus a fifth, and the priest is the one named to receive it. The same verse says the priest makes atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering, so the priest is the person to remember here.

I see why you'd think that, friend. Elders sound like important people to hand something to. But the text says he gives it "…to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering…" (Leviticus 5:16). The elders aren't mentioned in this verse at all.

Close, baker, but the Levites aren't in this verse. It names one person to receive the payment, and it's the priest (Leviticus 5:16). The text says he gives the value plus a fifth "…to the priest…" Remember it like this: the priest takes the payment, and the priest makes the atonement.

I can see the thinking, friend, since the priest is the one handling the offering. But the verse doesn't name him here. It says the man "…acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor…" (Leviticus 6:2). The one named as the target of the unfaithfulness is the LORD.
